brands.name: Michael Saggus Shapes
brands.short_description: Hand-shaped Australian surfboards by Michael Saggus on the NSW South Coast — fishes, midlengths, gliders, and involvement-era longboards built from Australian blanks.

models.name: Egg
models.description: This board now comes with a flat deck, low profile beak nose and refined foiled rails. The bottom transitions from flat to double concave through the tail and the rocker is flatter with an accelerated tail kick. Countless fin combos that now include a twinzer! This is a true Summer all-rounder. Length range 5’8” – 6’8” Fin set-up . Twin, twinzer, 2+1 or quad.

models.name: Saggus Fish
models.description: A fresh take on the classic fish, this board will fly over the flat spots and hold the high line through critical sections. It packs a lot of stoke into a small package. It features full down rails, a beak nose, low rocker, and a concave vee in the tail. From tiny to head high, the Saggus Fish will see you through most conditions with style. Riding a fish is always a rush, something every surfer should experience. Length range 5' 4” – 6’ 2" (Shorter is good.) Fin set-up Glass-on keels in either bamboo, ply or fibreglass

models.name: Long Fish
models.description: A drawn-out version of our fish design, this board is a high-octane alternative for surfers seeking something beyond their standard 2+1 experience. The Long Fish has a slightly straighter outline and increased rocker and features a beak nose, down rails and a deep concave toward the fins. Good for anyone intermediate or above, the Long Fish will have you grinning in most wave conditions. Length range 7’-9’ Fin set-up Twin, Thruster or Quad

models.name: Mini Simmons
models.description: Derived from the original Bob Simmons theory, the Mini Simmons is a great board to keep your surfing fresh. It features a scooped-out deck in the nose, a low rocker and rails that transition from 50/50 to hard in the tail. Basically it’s a hull with a concave between the fins. Ride it 6 to 8 inches shorter than your regular short board. Rips through steep sections and glides over flats. Simplicity with function, great to grab ’n’ go (or your standby board stashed in the trunk of your car). Length range 5' 2” – 6’ Fin set-up Simmons’ keels in wood or fibreglass. Glass-on or boxes

models.name: Long Simmons
models.description: Evolving from the planing shapes of Californian surfboard design pioneer Bob Simmons, this model incorporates the concave bottom-contour, rocker, foil, rail profiles and dual-fin innovations which revolutionised surfing way back when. Simmons was obsessed with speed and control, and this namesake design recreates his breakthrough in a board that planes faster, longer and more responsively. Decades ahead of its time, the Simmons design opened all the wave-riding doors that made modern surfing possible. Our version heads straight for the future! Length range 7’-8’6” Fin set-up Simmons’ keels in wood or fibreglass. Glass-on or boxes.

models.name: Pintail
models.description: At first glance, it’s a traditional pin with the wide point forward and a pulled in tail, yet the bottom tells a different story with a modern rocker and slight concave leading into a concave, spiral-vee. Good for smoothing out those turns, as only a pintail can and, with a Greenough style flex fin and that spiral vee, you can still drive hard. Optional side bites give extra drive off the bottom and grab off the top (shaper preferred). Perfect for those looking to experience the smooth, clean, ride of a well-designed pin, or for those who already know! Length range 6 4" – 7'8" Fin set-up Single (with optional sidebite fins)

models.name: Spider Bomb
models.description: Part of our more performance orientated line up. It has a wide point forward, round tail, flat deck and low rails, single concave to spiral vee. Perfect in long walls but with enough rocker to still go vertical. It’s ideal for when the surf is pumping and makes for a great travelling board – it’ll handle pretty much any decent wave you’ll find. Length range 5’10” – 6’ 10” Fin set-up Quad/Twin/Twinzer – your choice

models.name: Edge
models.description: Two boards in one! Conceived by George Greenough in the late 1960s and subsequently advanced by Marc Andreini, over time the Edge has made its way into the mainstream. In essence, the deck of a standard board (of your choice) with a narrower under-storey planing surface – the edge. It sounds wild, it looks wild. And it IS wild in the water. The Edge has been a personal journey for me – I love the challenge of the design and shaping process and the blast I get from surfing them. Try a demo board then talk to us. Custom only. Length range Any length depending on the board. Fin set-up Best with True Ames Power Blades (low aspect fins). Works well as a twin.

models.name: Middy
models.description: The Middy is a high-performance mid length for those slightly more demanding days. With slightly more rocker than Da Pig, it has a wide point and volume forward of centre, medium full rails at the middle, foiling to thin in the tail for speed and bite. Some use it as a ‘Step Up’ and others as a ‘Step Down’. It can turn harder and hold in tighter than most mid-lengths. Drop late, turn hard, shift weight forward and hang on! Length range 6’10” – 7’8” Fin set-up 2+1

models.name: Dru Pat
models.description: Built to perform on big clean open faces, you can paddle out with confidence on this beauty and experience unfettered speed and control. The design incorporates a flat deck with medium-down rails, natural rocker and a bottom contour featuring a soft chined entry heading to a flat panel vee to flat aft of the fins. There’s an obvious paddling advantage, allowing you to get in early, while the unique plan shape will let you draw long lines or power into turns. Quick and responsive underfoot, it’s ready to go when you are. Length range a bit either side of 7’5” Fin set-up Quad

models.name: Round Nose Pin
models.description: The low entry rocker, full nose and volume slightly forward, make this model a real wave catcher, helping you plane and glide over those pesky dead spots. Other features include medium down rails, a concave bottom transitioning to double under the back foot providing power through turns and cutbacks. Sizing is best a couple of inches shorter than rider’s height. Perfect for having some fun on head high waves. Length range . 5’ 10” – 6’ 10” Fin set-up Quad, twin or twinzer.

models.name: Performer
models.description: The plan shape says throw me around, I’m up for anything! With its full nose, wide point slightly forward of centre and narrow round tail, the Performer is ready to do your bidding. The bottom contour includes a steep, short concave up front easing to flat and then into a spiral vee in the tail, the rocker includes a little extra nose lift and the rails are low 60/40 to hard around the fins. As the name suggests, the Performer is more forgiving and more responsive than traditional longboard designs, and especially rewarding for intermediate to advanced surfers. Drive from take-off, run up to the nose to stall, run back to pivot and crank that cutback. Perform! Length range 9’1”+ Fin set-up 2+1

models.name: Gun
models.description: This Gun features a continuous bottom curve with accelerated nose rocker. The bottom contour starts with a moderate vee under the nose, softening to nearly flat at the widest point, before reverting to a deep spiral concave vee through the fin section. The rails are low and full without being ‘corky’ and are designed around a surfer’s weight, surf conditions, style etc. All of the above, combined with the Gun’s fine, continuous plan shape make for a board that handles late drops and strong winds, maintaining drive and acceleration out of turns in the most challenging of conditions. All boards have quality stringers and are glassed somewhat heavier than average boards. Length range 7’6’ - 10’ Fin set-up Tri-fin or Quad

models.name: Vee
models.description: The vee bottom fell out of favour when it was pushed to radical extremes in the late 1960s. Well, we’ve rehabilitated it! Modern rocker, refined rails and better volume distribution make our new vee bottom an exciting hot-dog option. The bottom is slightly rolled, with a rolled vee flattening behind the fin. The rails are medium 50/50 elliptical, it has a slightly rolled deck and maintains the traditional wide point aft of centre. Choose an arc or diamond tail. Forget those sixties Plastic Machines – our Vee finally delivers the lost promise of the vee bottom. Length range 7’6” – 9’ Fin set-up Single: Glass on or box. We recommend a glassed-on high-aspect 10’½” fibreglass fin.

models.name: Mini Glider
models.description: How about a board that has most of the attributes of a glider, without all that length? The key to the Mini Glider is the commitment in design to planing area – that neutral rocker, slightly lower rails, and a soft hull-design that allows easy rail to rail transition. A more compact package that converts to speed and freedom. Length 9’ to 10’ Fin set-up Single/2+1

models.name: Glider
models.description: When the waves have eased in size but are still clean and peeling, and maybe a bit fast for your regular board, it’s time to break out the Glider. The extra length is just the beginning. The parallel-rail plan shape, the slight rocker, the forgiving rails and the sophisticated bottom contour all make for a planing machine that takes off like a rocket and holds in the pocket all the way to the sand. If you know how to handle yourself in the line-up, the Glider will increase your wave count and introduce you to a new dimension of speed and momentum. Tail shape Square or pin. Length range . 10’6”–11’6” Fin set-up . Single/2+1

models.name: D Fin
models.description: Old style longboard cool with the classic pig outline, narrow nose and generous hips set back of centre. Low, low rocker throughout and a little non-traditional nose flip just to keep it friendly. Rails are elliptical nose to tail complementing the rolled bottom and deck. Hot dog and trim in traditional style for days. Length range 9’1” – 10’ Fin set-up D Fin Box, glass-on best.

models.name: Monumental
models.description: This shape has consistently proved a winner, and has established itself as our most popular longboard model. It embraces our Australian heritage from the late 1960s (Nat Young, the “Involvement” era), but with modern-day improvements. It features a full, generously-hipped outline with a pulled-in tail (choice of square or pin) for easier turning. There’s a long nose concave embedded in the softly rolled bottom, the rocker is low with a generous tail kick, and the rails are 60/40. This board can take your surfing to the next level! Length range 9’1” – 10’ Fin set-up Single fin: glass-on or box. Your choice.

models.name: Stepdeck
models.description: One of our most popular models; it features a full nose, generous hips and (you guessed it) a stepped deck! This lightens the nose, allowing faster swing response through turns and in tricky conditions. Rails transition from 50/50 forward to low through the middle and the tail (your choice of either square or pin). A concave vee in front of the fin with flat behind, along with moderate tail kick provides manoeuvrability and speed, whether it be for styling your best drop-knee turns or just weaving through a crowd. A great board for all! Length range . 9'0" – 10'2" Fin set-up Single: glass-on or box.

models.name: Butt Head
models.description: This board is a huge nod to the heyday of nose riding in the early 1960s. Think U.S. models by Bob Purvey and Con, Challenger, Dave Sweet, Greek, Noll and Bing, to name a few. The Butt Head model features low rocker with accelerated flip through the tail to aid turning and fit the wave when perched on the tip. It has a rounded square nose with a concave bottom transitioning to a soft roll through to flat behind the fin. Rails are soft 50/50. Hang those toes! Length range 9' – 10' Fin set-up Single: glass on D-Fin, or box.

models.name: Da Pig
models.description: This is an extremely versatile, fun board. In the classic pig style, the wide point is back from the centre with low rocker throughout the whole board. Rails are medium 50/50 pinched. The bottom contour is soft, flat, to rolled aft for quick turning off the tail. Will glide forever. D-Fin is recommended for superior trimming and stability. Length range 9' – 10' Fin set-up Single: glass on D-Fin, or box.
